title: The Verb That Ghosted Me (Ser vs Estar)
style: playful indie pop, comedy rap fusion, 108 BPM, witty male and female duet, bouncy bass, laugh-track claps, language-learning anthem, EN/ES/FR codeswitch, classroom-friendly, hooky chorus, ukulele accents
lyrics:
[Verse 1 — EN, witty male lead]
I asked "to be" to stay but it conjugated away
Je suis, tu es, il est, but my plans ran away
I tried to text "I am yours" — got "I exist as a thing"
Spanish verb tense drama, the worst kind of fling

[Pre-Chorus — duet]
Ser for the essence, the soul, the core
Estar for the moment, the right-now floor
One says who you ARE, one says how you FEEL
The verb that ghosted me kept the receipts on read

[Chorus — 3-language spin, big harmonies]
To be or not to be (EN)
Ser o no ser, that's the key (ES)
Être ou ne pas être, mon ami (FR)
The verb that ghosted me-ee-ee!

[Verse 2 — EN/ES code-switch, female lead]
"I am hungry" — tengo hambre, not soy hambre, son
"Estoy cansada" tonight, mañana ya no
Permanent versus temporary, that's the whole game
Estar y ser, hermano, they ain't ever the same

[Bridge — laugh-track claps]
[laugh] in English
[risa] in Spanish
[rire] in French
Same joke, three tongues, one philosophical mess

[Final Chorus]
To be or not to be (EN)
Ser o no ser, that's the key (ES)
Être ou ne pas être, mon ami (FR)
The verb that ghosted me-ee-ee!

[Outro — spoken]
Soy a polyglot. Estoy confused. C'est la vie.
